_comment: Gestational diabetes. Same architecture as pneumonia and pre-eclampsia: shared core and obgyn skills carry the approach, dates, abdomen and pressure; the disease owns screening, the diabetic picture, and control-to-delivery reasoning. History and presentation skills live in the shared fragment and merge into the obgyn pack.

chapters.blurb: Age and weight set the probability before a symptom is mentioned

skill.particulars.demographics.expect: In a pregnant woman, age above the mid twenties, excess weight, South Asian background and a previous large baby together set a high pre-test probability before any glucose is measured. Record pre-pregnancy weight wherever possible: without it, later gain cannot be judged.

chapters.title: Patient particulars

chapters.blurb: Usually silent, so ask about risk, symptoms and the overlap warnings

skill.hx.obg.booking_lmp.expect: Fix dates first: last menstrual period, regularity, first-trimester dating scan, and the expected date of delivery. Every glucose value and every growth measurement is interpreted against this gestation, and uncertain dates unravel the whole pathway.

skill.hx.chief_complaints.expect: Expect referral after routine screening rather than a complaint: sugar found high on a scheduled test at around 30 weeks. Ask how it was found, which test, and what she was told, since an unlabeled value cannot be used.

chapters.title: History of the pregnancy so far

chapters.blurb: The background that sets the testing calendar

skill.hx.gestational.risk.expect: In this woman expect several risks together: excess weight, a previous very big baby with a difficult shoulder delivery, and a diabetic mother. Each alone raises suspicion; together they explain why booking testing with a repeat was due.

skill.hx.obg.previous_pregnancies.expect: Ask the birth weight and delivery details of every earlier child. A previous unusually large baby with shoulder difficulty predicts both recurrence and the delivery plan this time.

chapters.title: Past, personal, drug and family history

chapters.blurb: A well woman, and the measurements that matter more than the eye

skill.gen.edema.expect: Mild ankle swelling that clears overnight fits the gestation. Sudden swelling of face or hands does not: it points to pre-eclampsia travelling with the diabetes and changes urgency on the spot.

skill.gen.vitals.expect: Blood pressure with urine protein at every contact, since hypertension is the commonest companion. Weight against booking weight, since steep gain tracks with poor control. The rest of the vitals are usually normal, and saying so is part of the record.

chapters.title: General examination

chapters.blurb: Fundal height, liquor, lie and the fetal heart

skill.exam.obg.fetal_heart.expect: Usually normal, and its normality is worth stating. An abnormal trace reflects placental compromise and overrides everything the glucose diary says.

skill.exam.obg.fundal_height.expect: Expect fundal height ahead of dates, reflecting a large fetus, extra liquor, or both. Measure against certain dates, then assess size and liquor separately rather than recording ahead and moving on.

skill.exam.obg.leopold.expect: Expect a large but normally formed fetus, usually cephalic, with the head high and ballotable where extra liquor is present. Confirm presentation: it decides what delivery options exist.

name: Gestational diabetes
oneLine: Glucose intolerance first found in pregnancy: screening, control and delivery planning

examinerQuestions: Demonstrate how you date this pregnancy from her last period and scan, and explain why every later measurement depends on it.
Name the risk factors you found and state when you would have tested her at booking and afterwards.
Her booking test was normal but risk persists. What is your screening plan from here?
stations.task: This 28-year-old woman is newly pregnant and her first baby was very big with a difficult delivery. Take a focused risk history and state when and how you would test her for diabetes.
stations.title: Risk history and screening plan

examinerQuestions: Present your fundal height, liquor and lie findings in one minute.
How do your findings change the timing and mode of delivery?
Name two neonatal problems you are preparing for and what you have arranged for each.
stations.task: This woman is 32 weeks pregnant with newly diagnosed gestational diabetes. Examine her abdomen and present fetal size, liquor and what they mean for delivery.
stations.title: Examine the diabetic abdomen and plan delivery

skill.gdm.basics.body: Gestational diabetes is glucose intolerance that is first recognised during pregnancy, distinct from diabetes that predates conception and is merely unmasked by antenatal testing.
keyPoints: Pregnancy is a progressively insulin-resistant state, driven by placental hormones, and diabetes appears when the maternal pancreas cannot make enough extra insulin to compensate.
Glucose crosses the placenta freely while maternal insulin does not, so the fetus makes its own extra insulin, which acts as a growth factor and drives excessive growth and fat deposition.
After the cord is cut the maternal glucose supply stops but the neonatal insulin level stays high for hours, which is why the baby of a diabetic mother is prone to low glucose soon after birth.

Most mothers return to normal glucose tolerance after delivery, yet face a substantially increased lifetime risk of type 2 diabetes, and their children face higher rates of obesity and glucose intolerance.

The fetal risks cluster together: excessive growth, extra liquor, shoulder injury at birth, breathing difficulty, low glucose, extra red cells with jaundice, and, when control is very poor, stillbirth.
Well controlled disease has an outcome approaching that of the non-diabetic population, so the whole pathway is about achieving control early and holding it.
skill.gdm.basics.oneLine: Glucose intolerance first found in pregnancy, driven by the placenta
pitfalls: Labelling diabetes that predates conception as gestational, which misses the need to look for established complications.
Assuming a normal-sized fetus means the neonate is safe from low glucose.
Assuming delivery ends the story for the mother, when her lifetime risk has just risen.

probes.a: Glucose intolerance first recognised during pregnancy, distinct from pre-existing diabetes that is merely unmasked by antenatal testing.
probes.q: Define gestational diabetes.

probes.a: Maternal glucose crosses the placenta and drives the fetus to make extra insulin, which acts as a growth factor causing excessive growth before birth and low glucose after the cord is cut.
probes.q: Why does one maternal problem cause both a large baby and a low neonatal glucose?

probes.a: Because most mothers return to normal tolerance after delivery yet carry a substantially increased lifetime risk of type 2 diabetes, so postpartum retesting and long-term follow-up are part of the disease, not an extra.
probes.q: Why is postpartum glucose testing part of this disease rather than an optional extra?

teach.body: The defining feature is timing: intolerance of glucose that shows up for the first time while she is pregnant. Diabetes found at booking in a woman with strong risk factors is more likely to predate the pregnancy, and calling it gestational understates both the fetal exposure so far and the need to look for established disease. The label is therefore a working one until early testing sorts the two apart.
teach.heading: First recognised in pregnancy

teach.body: Think of two patients at once. The fetus sits in extra glucose, grows too fast, and makes too much insulin. The mother sits in the same extra glucose and heads toward lifelong diabetes. Every step of management serves both: control protects the baby now, and surveillance with counselling protects the mother for decades.
teach.heading: Two patients, one disease

teach.body: Outcome follows control, not the label. A mother whose glucose stays within target through diet, monitoring and timely drugs can expect an outcome close to the non-diabetic population. A mother whose control slips faces a large baby, extra liquor, a difficult delivery and a sick neonate. That gap is the whole argument for screening, and for acting on the result without delay.
teach.heading: Control decides the outcome

skill.gdm.basics.title: What gestational diabetes is
skill.gdm.basics.why: The label decides two things at once: the baby is exposed to extra glucose right now, and the mother carries a high lifetime risk of diabetes afterwards. Confusing it with diabetes that predates pregnancy misses both the urgency of fetal surveillance and the need for postpartum retesting.

skill.gdm.findings.body: The bedside picture in gestational diabetes is usually a well woman with a large abdomen: fundal height ahead of dates, extra liquor, a big but normally formed fetus, and often raised weight and pressure. Normal findings elsewhere do not reassure on their own.
keyPoints: Weight: excess pre-pregnancy weight and steep gain, the visible end of the strongest modifiable risk.
Blood pressure and urine protein: hypertension travels with diabetes, and new raised pressure with proteinuria is pre-eclampsia until proved otherwise.
Fundal height ahead of dates: the single most useful bedside clue, reflecting a large fetus, extra liquor, or both.
Liquor: a full, tense uterus that is difficult to ballot through, with fluid thrill where extra liquor is marked.
Fetal size and lie: a ballotable large fetus, usually cephalic; confirm presentation, since malpresentation complicates the delivery decision.
Fetal heart: usually normal; an abnormal trace reflects placental compromise and overrides everything else.
What is absent: the mother usually looks well, which is exactly why the tape measure and the pressure gauge matter more than the eye.
skill.gdm.findings.oneLine: Often a normal woman; the findings are fetal size, liquor, pressure and weight
pitfalls: Calling the examination normal because the mother looks well, while the fundal height sits weeks ahead of dates.
Missing coexisting pre-eclampsia because attention stopped at the glucose value.
Confusing extra liquor with a large fetus without assessing each separately.

probes.a: A well mother with fundal height ahead of dates, extra liquor, a large fetus, excess weight, and often raised blood pressure.
probes.q: Describe the typical bedside picture in gestational diabetes.

probes.a: Because hypertension travels with diabetes in pregnancy, and new raised pressure with proteinuria is pre-eclampsia until proved otherwise.
probes.q: Why is blood pressure part of every review in a diabetic pregnancy?

probes.a: Assess fetal size and liquor separately: ballottement and grip findings for the fetus, and uterine tension with fluid thrill for the liquor, since each changes the delivery decision differently.
probes.q: Fundal height is four weeks ahead of dates. How do you sort out why?

teach.body: Expect a well woman, not a sick one. Gestational diabetes rarely makes the mother look ill, so the student waiting for a sick patient will walk past the diagnosis. The disease declares itself through the tape measure, the weighing scale and the pressure gauge, not through the general appearance.
teach.heading: A well woman, not a sick one
What to find, in order
points: Weight and build: excess weight and steep gain since booking.
Pressure and urine protein: raised values mean a second disease until proved otherwise.
Fundal height against dates: ahead means a large fetus, extra liquor, or both.
Liquor assessment: uterine tension and ease of feeling fetal parts.
Fetal grip findings and presentation: size, lie and engagement.
Fetal heart: normal is expected, abnormal overrides all else.

teach.body: Fundal height ahead of dates is the finding students most often record without acting on. An abdomen measuring weeks ahead needs same-visit assessment of fetal size and liquor, not a note to recheck next month. By the next visit the window for adjusting the delivery plan has narrowed, and a large baby has only grown larger.
teach.heading: Act on the tape measure

skill.gdm.findings.title: The gestational diabetes picture
skill.gdm.findings.why: The examination in gestational diabetes rewards measurement over impression: the mother usually looks well while the uterus measures large. Knowing which measurements matter, fundal height against dates, liquor state, pressure and weight, turns a routine antenatal check into the visit that sets the delivery plan.

skill.gdm.screening.body: Screening rests on glucose tolerance testing around 24 to 28 weeks for every pregnant woman, with earlier testing for women with risk factors and retesting when the first test is normal but risk persists.
keyPoints: Test every pregnant woman around 24 to 28 weeks with a glucose tolerance test using fasting and post-load values, the window when placental resistance peaks.
Test high-risk women at booking: a normal result then does not close the question, and testing is repeated in the screening window.
Measure HbA1c early when prior diabetes is suspected; it helps separate overt pre-existing diabetes from true gestational disease.

Where a formal multi-sample tolerance test is impractical, a single-step non-fasting glucose challenge, as used in Indian practice, keeps screening within reach; the threshold and pathway are set by the current national guidance.
Record weight, blood pressure and urine protein alongside every test, since hypertension and kidney disease change both diagnosis and urgency.
Document which test was done at what gestation: an unlabeled glucose value later is uninterpretable.
skill.gdm.screening.oneLine: Universal screening around mid pregnancy, earlier when risk is high
pitfalls: Testing only women with symptoms, when most affected women feel entirely well.
Treating one normal early test as ruling out disease in a high-risk woman.
Acting on a single random glucose value instead of a proper tolerance test.
Recording a glucose value without the test name and gestation, making it useless later.

probes.a: Every pregnant woman is tested around 24 to 28 weeks with a glucose tolerance test using fasting and post-load values, and high-risk women are tested at booking with a repeat in the screening window.
probes.q: Who is tested for gestational diabetes, and when?

probes.a: Because waiting until mid pregnancy leaves overt diabetes untreated while the fetal organs are forming, so early testing with a repeat later covers both overt and gestational disease.
probes.q: Why test a high-risk woman at booking instead of waiting for the screening window?

probes.a: HbA1c measured early helps separate overt pre-existing diabetes from true gestational disease, so a high value redirects the woman to full diabetic assessment rather than routine gestational management.
probes.q: What does an early HbA1c add to the glucose tolerance test?

sources.locator: Classification of hyperglycaemia first detected in pregnancy
sources.source: WHO guidance on hyperglycaemia in pregnancy

teach.body: Two calendars run together. Every woman is screened around 24 to 28 weeks, when placental hormones push resistance to its peak. Women with risk factors are tested at booking as well, because their diabetes may predate the pregnancy and the fetus cannot wait until mid pregnancy for treatment. One normal early test never closes the question in this group.
teach.heading: Two calendars, not one

rows: At booking, repeated at 24 to 28 weeks
May be overt diabetes; fetus cannot wait
Resistance peaks; one test suffices when normal
Previous normal early test, risk persists

teach.body: A glucose value without its context is clutter. Fasting, post-load, random and HbA1c each answer a different question, and a bare number copied into the notes without the test name and gestation cannot be interpreted weeks later when the diagnosis is reviewed. Insist on labelled values, and use the single-step non-fasting challenge where a formal tolerance test is beyond reach, following national guidance.
teach.heading: Label every value

skill.gdm.screening.title: Finding it: who to test, when, and how
skill.gdm.screening.why: Symptoms miss nearly every case, so the screening plan is the diagnostic tool. Getting the timing wrong in either direction harms: testing only at mid pregnancy leaves overt diabetes untreated through organ formation, while never testing the standard-risk woman misses the commonest form of the disease.

skill.gdm.summary.body: State the woman with the risk factors that matter, the gestation and how glucose intolerance was found, the fetal size and liquor state, the blood pressure, and control so far, in that order.
keyPoints: Name the woman with the risk factors that drive this pregnancy: age, weight, previous large baby, family history.
State the gestation and how intolerance was found: which test, at what gestation, and whether overt diabetes is excluded.
State the fetal state: growth, liquor, movements, and presentation where known.
Include blood pressure and urine protein in the same summary, since coexisting hypertension changes the plan.
State control so far: diet, monitoring, drugs, and whether targets are met.

A worked example: a 29 year old second pregnancy at 30 weeks with glucose intolerance on routine screening and a previous large baby. Fundal height ahead of dates with extra liquor, blood pressure normal, fasting glucose above target despite diet. This is gestational diabetes with fetal overgrowth, needing tightened control and a delivery plan.
skill.gdm.summary.oneLine: Risk, gestation, fetal state, pressure and control in one paragraph
pitfalls: Quoting glucose values without the test and gestation that produced them.
Omitting blood pressure, leaving the listener unable to judge urgency.
Summarising the mother without the fetus, when the delivery plan depends on both.

probes.a: The risk factors, the gestation with how intolerance was found, the fetal size and liquor state, the blood pressure, and control so far.
probes.q: What five elements belong in the gestational diabetes summary?

probes.a: Because the delivery decision depends on fetal size and liquor as much as on glucose, so a summary without the fetus cannot support a plan.
probes.q: Why does the summary carry fetal details that a diabetes summary outside pregnancy would not?

rubric.text: States the woman with relevant risk factors
States fetal size, liquor and pressure
States control so far and what it demands

teach.body: The summary for this disease has two subjects, and students habitually report only one. The mother brings risk, gestation and control; the fetus brings size, liquor and movements; the pressure reading belongs to both. Leave any of the three out and the listener cannot reach a delivery decision, which is the entire point of gathering them.
teach.heading: Two subjects, one summary

teach.body: Fix the order and keep it: woman with risk, gestation with test, fetal state, pressure, control. Practise it until it runs under a minute. The worked example in the key points shows the shape: each clause earns its place by changing the plan, and nothing is narrated twice.
teach.heading: The fixed order

skill.gdm.summary.title: The clinical summary
skill.gdm.summary.why: The summary is where the delivery decision starts forming, so it must carry everything that decision needs: maternal risk, gestation, fetal size and liquor, pressure, and control. A summary that reports glucose values without the fetus leaves the listener with numbers and no plan.

skill.gdm.diagnosis.body: Confirm glucose intolerance first found in the current pregnancy, exclude overt pre-existing diabetes, and state the diagnosis with its basis, gestation, fetal state and control, since each changes the plan.
keyPoints: Gestational diabetes: glucose intolerance first recognised in this pregnancy on tolerance testing around 24 to 28 weeks, or earlier in a high-risk woman with previously normal testing.

Overt diabetes in pregnancy: intolerance that predates conception, suggested by very high values, early onset, or raised early HbA1c; it needs full diabetic assessment, not routine gestational management.
A complete diagnostic statement names the condition, the test and gestation behind it, the fetal size and liquor state, blood pressure, and control so far.
Coexisting hypertension with proteinuria alongside the diabetes is pre-eclampsia as well, and is stated as a second diagnosis, not folded into the first.
Uncertainty is stated, not hidden: where early testing was never done, say whether overt disease is excluded or still open.
skill.gdm.diagnosis.oneLine: Gestational or overt, stated with test, gestation, fetus and control
pitfalls: Calling overt diabetes gestational because it was first noticed antenatally.
Stating the diagnosis without the test and gestation, so nobody can judge its basis.
Folding coexisting pre-eclampsia into the diabetes label instead of diagnosing it separately.

probes.a: Glucose intolerance first recognised in the current pregnancy on tolerance testing, with overt pre-existing diabetes excluded by early testing and HbA1c.
probes.q: What must be true before you label hyperglycaemia in pregnancy as gestational?

probes.a: Very high values, onset in early pregnancy, or a raised early HbA1c suggest diabetes that predates conception, needing full diabetic assessment rather than routine gestational management.
probes.q: Which features suggest overt rather than gestational diabetes?

probes.a: No. New raised pressure with proteinuria alongside the diabetes is pre-eclampsia as well, and missing it because the glucose explained the visit is dangerous.
probes.q: A diabetic woman at 34 weeks develops raised pressure with proteinuria. Is the diabetes explanation enough?

rubric.text: States the test and gestation behind the label
Shows overt diabetes was considered and excluded or pursued
Adds fetal state, pressure and control to the statement

teach.body: Two labels cover all new hyperglycaemia in pregnancy, and they point in different directions. Gestational disease follows the screening calendar with diet, monitoring and timely drugs. Overt disease needs the full apparatus of diabetes care: eyes, kidneys, heart, and tighter targets from the start. The discriminator is history and early testing, not the size of one value.
teach.heading: Two labels, two pathways

teach.body: A diagnosis that cannot be audited is an opinion. State which test was above threshold, at what gestation, and what excluded overt disease. Weeks later, when control slips or the fetus grows fast, the team replays exactly this statement to decide whether the label still holds. Write it so they can.
teach.heading: Make the diagnosis auditable

skill.gdm.diagnosis.title: Diagnosis: gestational or overt
skill.gdm.diagnosis.why: The word gestational reassures, which is why it must be earned: overt diabetes mislabelled as gestational receives lighter surveillance than it needs. A diagnosis that states its basis, excludes overt disease, and carries the fetal state and control alongside it is the only one the delivery plan can safely rest on.

skill.gdm.differential.body: For high glucose in pregnancy, work through overt diabetes of each type, impaired tolerance that predates conception, drug-induced rises, and uncommon single-gene forms, while carrying coexisting hypertension and infection as parallel problems.
keyPoints: Overt type 2 diabetes unmasked by pregnancy: favoured by excess weight, strong family history, very high values, and onset in early pregnancy.
Overt type 1 diabetes: favoured by younger age, lean build, rapid onset with weight loss, ketones, and a short history.
Impaired glucose tolerance predating pregnancy: favoured by previous borderline values or a history of polycystic ovary syndrome with long-standing irregular cycles.
Steroid or stress-induced rise: favoured by recent corticosteroids for threatened preterm labour or another illness, with previously normal values.
Monogenic diabetes: favoured by young onset with a strong three-generation family pattern; uncommon, but changes counselling for the child.
Coexisting pre-eclampsia: not an alternative to diabetes but its frequent companion; new hypertension with proteinuria is diagnosed alongside, never instead.
Urinary or genital infection: favoured by burning, discharge or fever; infection both unmasks poor control and worsens it, so it is sought and treated.
skill.gdm.differential.oneLine: Overt, drug-induced and single-gene mimics, with hypertension and infection alongside
pitfalls: Assuming every high value in pregnancy is gestational without asking about onset and prior values.
Missing steroid-induced rises in a woman recently treated for threatened preterm labour.
Treating infection as irrelevant to glucose when it both signals and worsens poor control.

probes.a: Overt type 1 and type 2 diabetes, impaired tolerance predating pregnancy, steroid-induced rises, and uncommon monogenic forms, with coexisting pre-eclampsia and infection as parallel problems.
probes.q: Name the differential for high glucose newly found in pregnancy.

probes.a: Recently given corticosteroids for threatened preterm labour with previously normal values favour a drug-induced rise, which is managed by watching glucose closely through the steroid course rather than relabelling her disease.
probes.q: A woman with normal booking tests runs high glucose a week after steroids for threatened preterm labour. What is favoured?

teach.body: Two conditions sit alongside the differential rather than inside it. Hypertension with proteinuria is diagnosed as well as diabetes, never instead of it. Infection of the urine or genital tract both reveals and worsens poor control, so it is actively sought at every visit. Students lose marks by forcing these into an either-or list.
teach.heading: Alongside, not instead

skill.gdm.differential.title: Differential diagnosis
skill.gdm.differential.why: Most high glucose in pregnancy is exactly what it looks like, but the exceptions change everything: overt disease needs heavier care, a drug-induced rise needs watching rather than relabelling, and coexisting hypertension missed because the glucose explained the visit can kill. The differential protects against all three errors at once.

skill.ix.gdm.workup.body: Group investigations by what they answer: confirm the intolerance, grade day-to-day control, exclude overt disease, watch the fetus, and catch the companions.
keyPoints: CONFIRM: glucose tolerance testing with fasting and post-load values around 24 to 28 weeks, or earlier in high risk; document test and gestation with every value.
GRADE CONTROL: home capillary monitoring of fasting and post-meal values to steer therapy; control is judged on the diary, not on one clinic value.
EXCLUDE OVERT DISEASE: HbA1c measured early helps separate pre-existing diabetes from true gestational disease.
WATCH THE FETUS: serial growth ultrasound for excessive growth with measurement of liquor volume; extra liquor and a large abdominal circumference change the delivery plan.
CATCH THE COMPANIONS: blood pressure with urine protein at every contact, and urine culture where burning or repeated infection suggests it.
CLOSE THE LOOP: postpartum tolerance testing to reclassify glucose status, since most mothers normalise but many return diabetic within years.
The single most important principle: never let the wait for a confirmatory test delay diet, monitoring and referral in a woman whose values are already clearly high.
skill.ix.gdm.workup.oneLine: Confirm it, grade control, exclude overt disease, watch the fetus
pitfalls: Judging control from one clinic value instead of the home diary.
Repeating the tolerance test to confirm when values are already clearly high, delaying management.
Never arranging postpartum retesting, so persistent diabetes surfaces years later.
Ordering growth scans without assessing liquor, or liquor without growth, when each changes the plan.

probes.a: Tolerance testing with fasting and post-load values confirms it; home capillary monitoring of fasting and post-meal values grades control; early HbA1c helps exclude overt disease.
probes.q: Which test confirms, which grades control, and which excludes overt disease?

probes.a: Serial growth ultrasound with liquor assessment, because excessive growth with extra liquor changes the timing and mode of delivery.
probes.q: What fetal surveillance does a diabetic pregnancy need, and why?

probes.a: Start diet, monitoring and referral on the clearly high values without waiting; the confirmatory test follows but never gates management.
probes.q: Values are clearly high but the confirmatory test is a week away. What do you do?

sources.source: NICE guideline on diabetes in pregnancy

teach.body: Each test answers one question, and ordering without the question wastes the visit. The tolerance test asks whether intolerance exists. The home diary asks how bad today is. Early HbA1c asks whether this predates the pregnancy. Growth ultrasound with liquor assessment asks what the fetus has suffered so far. Postpartum testing asks what remains. Teach students to state the question before the test.
teach.heading: One test, one question

teach.body: Postpartum retesting is the investigation most often never ordered. Most mothers normalise after delivery, which feels like cure and breeds complacency, yet a large share return with diabetes within years. The six-week reclassification visit is where lifelong prevention starts, with weight, feeding, activity and family planning counselled together.
teach.heading: Do not lose her after delivery

skill.ix.gdm.workup.title: Investigations
skill.ix.gdm.workup.why: Investigations in gestational diabetes serve five separate jobs, confirming the diagnosis, grading control, excluding overt disease, watching the fetus, and catching hypertension and infection, and understanding which test does which stops a student repeating the tolerance test while the fetus keeps growing.

skill.tx.gdm.body: Begin with food, monitoring and activity for every woman, add drugs when targets are unmet with insulin preferred, watch the fetus throughout, plan delivery around size and liquor, guard the neonate, and retest the mother after birth.
skill.tx.gdm.dosingNote: This module teaches management at the level of drug CLASS and principle. Specific agents, regimens and targets must be taken from your current national or institutional guideline at the time of prescribing. CliniX does not prescribe.
keyPoints: Food first: medical nutrition therapy suited to Indian diets, with carbohydrate spread through the day rather than heaped into two meals, started at diagnosis for every woman.
Monitoring with movement: home capillary checks of fasting and post-meal values with regular walking as advised, reviewed against targets at each visit.
Drugs when targets are unmet: insulin is the preferred agent in pregnancy and metformin the alternative; the choice, regimen and target are set by current guidance, not memorised here.
Steroids with cover: where preterm birth threatens, antenatal corticosteroids are still given, with glucose watched closely and insulin adjusted under supervision.
Fetal watch: serial growth and liquor surveillance, with reduced movements or a non-reassuring trace prompting same-day review whatever the glucose shows.

Delivery planning: timing and mode set by control, fetal size, liquor and pressure; a large baby with extra liquor lowers the threshold for a planned delivery, and shoulder injury is explicitly prepared for.
Neonatal guard: early feeding with glucose monitoring of the baby, since low glucose in the first hours is expected, not surprising.

After birth: postpartum tolerance testing with counselling on weight, activity, breastfeeding, family planning and lifelong diabetes risk, coordinated across obstetrics, medicine, dietetics and neonatology.
Referral thresholds: poor control despite therapy, coexisting hypertension, suspected overgrowth with extra liquor, or reduced movements move her promptly to a higher centre with neonatal support.
skill.tx.gdm.oneLine: Food, monitoring and movement first; insulin preferred when targets slip; deliver by size
pitfalls: Leaving diet advice as eat less sugar instead of a structured carbohydrate plan.
Adding drugs late, after weeks above target have already grown the fetus.
Withholding steroids for threatened preterm birth from fear of glucose, instead of giving them with cover.
Discharging the neonate without glucose monitoring because the birth went smoothly.
Losing the mother after delivery without retesting or counselling.

probes.a: Medical nutrition therapy with home glucose monitoring and physical activity is first line, with insulin preferred and metformin alternative when targets are unmet.
probes.q: What is first-line management, and what comes next when targets are unmet?

probes.a: Give the steroids with close glucose watching and supervised insulin adjustment, because the neonatal benefit outweighs a transient rise that can be managed.
probes.q: Preterm labour threatens at 32 weeks in a diabetic pregnancy. Steroids or not?

probes.a: Timing and mode follow control, fetal size, liquor and pressure; a large baby with extra liquor lowers the threshold for planned delivery with shoulder injury prepared for.
probes.q: How do size and liquor change the delivery plan?

sources.source: NICE guideline on diabetes in pregnancy

teach.body: Every woman starts with the same three measures: a structured food plan built around her own diet, home glucose checks that she brings to each visit, and regular walking. Drugs enter only when these miss target, and the order is fixed: insulin first, metformin as the alternative. The steps are sequential, not a menu, and skipping ahead without giving food and monitoring time to work is poor care.
teach.heading: Steps in order, not a menu

teach.body: Delivery is planned, not awaited. Control, fetal size, liquor volume and blood pressure together set the timing and the mode, and a large baby with extra liquor moves both earlier. At every delivery in a diabetic pregnancy the team prepares explicitly for shoulder injury, with manoeuvres and help at hand before they are needed. Hope is not a plan for shoulders.
teach.heading: Plan the birth around size

teach.body: In Indian practice much of this pathway runs through the front line: the village health worker who brings her back for testing, the medical officer who starts diet and monitoring, and timely referral to the district hospital when control slips, pressure rises, or the fetus outgrows the plan. State the referral reason on the slip, send the glucose diary with her, and never refer without stabilising what can be stabilised first.
teach.heading: Run it through the system

skill.tx.gdm.title: Managing gestational diabetes
skill.tx.gdm.why: Management fails in predictable places: diet advice too vague to follow, drugs added too late, steroids withheld from fear, shoulders unprepared at delivery, and the mother lost after birth. A fixed sequence run through the available system, with explicit referral thresholds, prevents each of these without needing any new facility.

differentialModel.answer: Gestational diabetes mellitus with macrosomia and polyhydramnios. Consider pre-existing type 2 diabetes mellitus unmasked by pregnancy, type 1 diabetes mellitus, and coexisting pre eclampsia; a urinary tract infection may be worsening control. Steroid use is an alternative explanation for high glucose where relevant.

diagnosis.answer: Gestational diabetes mellitus at 30 weeks found on routine screening, with fetal macrosomia and polyhydramnios.

skill.exam.obg.fetal_heart.finding: Fetal heart regular at 142 per minute, no decelerations on auscultation.

skill.exam.obg.fundal_height.finding: Symphysis-fundal height 33 cm at 30 weeks by dates, measuring about three weeks ahead. Uterus tense with excess liquor; fetal parts difficult to feel clearly.

skill.exam.obg.leopold.finding: Single fetus, longitudinal lie, cephalic presentation. Fetal size large for dates with the head still high and ballotable above the brim.

skill.exam.obg.preg_prep_inspect.finding: Abdomen uniformly enlarged with striae and a midline linea nigra. No scar, no hernia, no visible veins. Privacy maintained with a female attendant present.

skill.gen.appearance.finding: Alert and comfortable, well nourished with central weight gain. No pallor of consequence, no breathlessness at rest.

skill.gen.edema.finding: Mild ankle swelling that pits slightly and clears overnight. No facial or hand swelling.

skill.gen.vitals.finding: Blood pressure 124/82. Pulse 88 regular. Respiratory rate 18. SpO2 98 percent on room air. Temperature 37.1 C. Weight above her booking weight with a steep rise since mid pregnancy.

cases.fallback: I am not sure what you mean, doctor. Can you ask that a different way?

cues: how many times have you come for checkup
anc_visits.reply: I come to this hospital for checkups since four months. They gave me iron tablets. Sugar was never tested before this month.

baby_movements.reply: Movements are present every day, doctor, but for the last week they feel slower than before.

belly_growth.reply: Yes, in the last one month my belly has grown very fast. My old clothes do not fit at all, and lying straight makes me breathless.

fainting_fits.reply: No fits, doctor, nothing like that has happened.

cues: anyone at home taking diabetes tablets
family_sugar.reply: My mother takes tablets for sugar since many years, and my elder brother was also told last year that his sugar is high.

cues: what do you eat in a day
sugary snacks and sweets in the daily meals
food_activity.reply: We eat rice twice a day with dal and vegetables, and tea with sugar three times. After marriage I do only housework, no walking outside.

head_vision_swelling.reply: No headache, no problem with vision, and no sudden swelling of the face. Only my feet swell a little by evening.

home_work.reply: I am a homemaker. I never use tobacco. My husband smokes bidis but only outside the house.

leaking_fluid.reply: No leaking of water till now, doctor.

pressure_thyroid.reply: No pressure problem and no thyroid problem. This is the first time any test of mine has come abnormal.

cues: what is the problem in this pregnancy
why have you been referred here
presenting.reply: Doctor, at thirty weeks they tested my blood for sugar and said it has come high. They sent me here saying the baby may grow too big.

cues: how was the first baby born
prior_pregnancy.reply: My first baby is a boy, now four years old. He was very big at birth and the delivery was difficult, they had to pull his shoulder. No abortion or loss before or after him.

steroid_drugs.reply: Only iron and calcium tablets, doctor. No other regular medicines.

cues: when was sugar first found high
sugar_timeline.reply: This month only, doctor. They took blood in the morning empty stomach and again after giving sweet water. Both were above normal, that is all they told me.

cues: feeling very thirsty with a dry mouth
thirst.reply: Yes, for the last two months I feel thirsty all the time and drink much more water than before.

thrush_boils.reply: For one month there is itching down below with thick white discharge. Passing urine burns a little also.

tiredness.reply: I feel tired the whole day, much more than in my first pregnancy at this stage.

cues: waking at night to pass urine
how many times urine at night
urine_nights.reply: I pass urine very often, and wake up three times at night only for this.

weight_before.reply: Before this pregnancy I was already heavy, and now I have put on a lot more. My sister says I have grown wider as well as bigger in front.

growth_us.label: Obstetric growth ultrasound
growth_us.note: Excessive growth with a large abdominal circumference moves the delivery plan earlier; growth and liquor are read together, never alone.
growth_us.result: Single live fetus, cephalic, parameters above the range for 30 weeks with the abdominal circumference the largest. No anomaly seen. Estimated weight above the ninetieth percentile.

hba1c.label: HbA1c
hba1c.note: Measured now it looks backwards: a clearly raised value points to diabetes that predates conception rather than true gestational disease.
hba1c.result: Mildly raised, in keeping with months of high glucose rather than years of overt diabetes.

home_profile.label: Home capillary glucose profile
home_profile.note: The diary, not one clinic value, judges control from here on and steers every drug decision.
home_profile.result: Fasting and post-meal values both above target on three consecutive days despite diet advice.

liquor_assess.label: Liquor volume assessment
liquor_assess.note: Extra liquor confirms the fetal effect of high glucose and, with a large baby, lowers the threshold for a planned delivery.
liquor_assess.result: Increased liquor volume with the deepest pool above normal. No septations. Placenta upper segment, normal grade.

ogtt.label: Oral glucose tolerance test
ogtt.note: This is the test that made the diagnosis: fasting with post-load values at the right gestation, labelled and filed.
ogtt.result: Done at 30 weeks: fasting value above threshold with raised post-load values, diagnostic of glucose intolerance first found in pregnancy.

repeat_ogtt.label: Repeat tolerance test next week
repeat_ogtt.note: Not indicated: repeating the test to confirm what is already clearly abnormal only delays diet, monitoring and referral by a week.

urine_routine.label: Urine routine and culture
urine_routine.note: Infection both reveals and worsens poor control, so it is sought and treated rather than assumed absent.
urine_routine.result: Sugar present, protein absent. Pus cells present; culture sent for urinary infection with thrush on perineal inspection.

managementModel.answer: Medical nutrition therapy with home glucose monitoring and daily walking; add insulin, preferred in pregnancy, if targets are unmet; serial growth and liquor surveillance with urine infection treated; a delivery plan accounting for macrosomia with shoulder injury prepared for; early feeding with neonatal glucose monitoring; and postpartum testing with counselling on future type 2 diabetes.

cases.opening: Sunita Patil, 29 years old, 30 weeks pregnant with her second child, has been referred from her antenatal clinic because her sugar test came high. Take her history.

patient.name: Sunita Patil
patient.residence: Semi-urban, lives with husband, son and mother-in-law near Satara

teachingPoints: The tempo and route of finding carry the diagnosis: routine screening at 30 weeks with no earlier testing, in a woman with a previous large baby and a diabetic mother, is the classic entry point.
A previous difficult shoulder delivery with a very big baby is doing double work: it predicts recurrence and it already argues for a planned delivery this time.
Fundal height weeks ahead of dates with a tense uterus and impalpable parts is extra liquor until assessed, not just a large baby, and each changes the plan.
Normal pressure with absent proteinuria is a relevant negative that must be stated, since hypertension is the commonest companion and its absence is doing real work.
Thrush with urinary burning is not a side complaint here: infection both signals and worsens poor control and must be treated as part of glycaemic management.
Postpartum retesting closes the loop for the mother, whose lifetime risk has just risen even as her glucose normalises after birth.
The neonate needs glucose monitoring despite a smooth birth, because maternal supply stops at cord clamping while fetal insulin stays high.
cases.title: Referred for high sugar at thirty weeks
